name: Greg Navarro

five_sec.what_is_it: Recipe app with meal plans and grocery lists. Kind of like Mealime maybe.
five_sec.who_for: People who cook a lot and save recipes.
five_sec.trust_why: Good ratings, no card for the trial. But 'trial' means it's not free.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Lists and recipes, person writing in a notebook.

full_page.what_stopped_me: $5.95 a month after 14 days, and they even have a question 'Why isn't there a free plan?' Mealime gave me recipes. This wants me to bring my own. I don't have recipes, that's the problem.
full_page.whats_missing: A free version. Recipes it gives me. An allergy setting.

PTE.quote: Nice app but I gotta bring my own recipes. If I had recipes I wouldn't be eating frozen pizza.

five_sec.what_is_it: Plans the week's dinners, the family votes by text, list goes to Walmart or Instacart.
five_sec.who_for: Parents who hate the 'what's for dinner' question. 👍
five_sec.trust_why: 'Start free, no card needed' right in the big button. Never heard of it though.
five_sec.next_step: Check if free is really free and if there's an allergy setting.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Says 'We don't deliver food' right under the paragraph.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Bit confused on the allergy thing. The home page lists allergies under the $4.99 Family plan, then the pricing page says nut allergies are respected on every plan. Which is it? Not trying to be the dad who slipped up on peanuts.
full_page.whats_missing: Clear answer that the peanut setting is on the free plan. Whether I can skip the weeks the kids are at their mom's.

DD.quote: '$0 forever,' Walmart cart, dinners under 20 minutes. That's basically Mealime. Just tell me straight the peanut thing is free too.

five_sec.what_is_it: An app that picks dinners for you.
five_sec.trust_why: 90,000 families sounds big. 'Letter from the CEO' button is weird, I just want to try it.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Menu on a phone, no delivery box.

full_page.what_stopped_me: There's a free plan, but it's 50 messages a month. I don't want to count texts. Paid is $25 a month, which is a couple fast food runs. And it's AI writing the recipes; not sure I trust it with peanuts.
full_page.whats_missing: Allergy setting. What 50 messages gets me in actual dinners.

OL.quote: Free, but you get 50 messages a month? Feels like a flip phone plan.

five_sec.trust_why: Big name, but the mystery box pop-up is a sales gimmick.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Boxes with the logo and food.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Need a zip code just to see prices, auto-renewing in the fine print, and half the menu has peanuts on it: candied peanuts, Thai salad with peanuts. Not with my youngest.
full_page.whats_missing: A price. A peanut-free filter I could see.

HF.quote: Candied peanuts, peanuts on the curry, peanuts on the bowls. Hard pass with a peanut kid.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal plans, I think. There's a video.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Phone with food pictures, could be an order app.

full_page.what_stopped_me: 14-day trial, then paid, and no price on the page. A pop-up wants my email. Kid Friendly plan looks good but I'm not paying for what used to be free.

EM.quote: Kid Friendly plan sounds good. But it's a trial with no price. Mealime never made me guess.

dd_offer.why: Free plan forever, the Family stuff is free 14 days, no card. Pretty easy.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: The family texting goes away and I'm on the free plan. Didn't give a card, so nothing gets charged.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one that's free like Mealime was, gives me the dinners and the Walmart list.

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat costs money and I have to bring my own recipes.

OL.reason: Ollie's free plan counts messages; DinnerDrop's free plan is unlimited plans.

HF.reason: HelloFresh is expensive boxes with peanuts all over the menu.

EM.reason: eMeals is a trial that turns paid; DinnerDrop is $0 forever.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Pricing page (/start) Free column: add a line like 'Allergy settings (peanut, dairy, gluten) included' so it's not only listed under the $4.99 Family plan. Right now the home page makes it look like allergies cost money.
